histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, provider) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_bucket{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])))

100 * avg by (provider) ( avg_over_time( ( (sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_sum{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_count{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval]))) == bool on (region) group_left() (min by (region) (sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_sum{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_count{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])))) )[1h:1m] ) )

panels.title: Win % by provider per region ($method)
panels.description: For the selected $method, each provider's share of the time it had the lowest avg latency, broken out per region. Computed from rpc_latency_seconds as rate(_sum)/rate(_count) per provider+region, compared against the per-region minimum (== bool on region group_left), averaged over the trailing hour.

targets.expr: 100 * avg by (provider, region) ( avg_over_time( ( (sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_sum{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_count{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval]))) == bool on (region) group_left() (min by (region) (sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_sum{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider, region) (rate(rpc_latency_seconds_count{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])))) )[1h:1m] ) )

panels.title: Success rate by provider ($method, $geo)
panels.description: Share of valid, fresh responses per provider. Errors and stale/cached data are excluded from the latency and win % panels, so a low value here means those panels are unreliable for that provider.

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (provider) (rate(rpc_requests_total{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="success"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider) (rate(rpc_requests_total{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status=~"success|error"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Error rate by provider ($method, $geo)
panels.description: Share of requests that errored per provider — timeouts, HTTP 4xx/429, rpc errors, empty/invalid, stale. Skipped-slot responses (JSON-RPC -32007/-32009 on getBlock at a slot the chain skipped) are a correct answer and excluded from both numerator and denominator. A provider missing from the latency/win panels is erroring; this shows why. Break down by error_kind on rpc_requests_total (e.g. http_429 = we are being rate-limited).

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (provider) (rate(rpc_requests_total{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status="error"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (provider) (rate(rpc_requests_total{infra=~"$infra", method="$method", geo=~"$geo", region=~"$region", provider=~"$provider", status=~"success|error"}[$__rate_interval])))
